blocks.text: Buy Bye was CON’s pop-up shop and installation for Jerusalem Design Week 2024, at Hansen House. A fictional Middle Eastern conglomerate set up shop in preparation for an impending flood or migration, offering a collection that moved between survival gear and luxury goods.

Cleaning supplies, clothing, printed cartons and everyday objects became vehicles for marketing, persuasion and casual propaganda. The shop brought CON’s fictional corporate world into a physical space, where familiar products carried unfamiliar promises.

blocks.text: The objects explored the tension between consumerism and crisis: how design, marketing and desire operate in times of uncertainty. Playful and unsettling at once, they asked whether the next thing we consume is a necessity, a reassurance or a facade.

blocks.text: Survival consumption runs through the collection. Packaging and branding turn national anxiety into things to take home, reflecting the contradictions of a culture that prepares for disaster through the language of abundance.

blocks.text: Under the guise of a functioning shop, Buy Bye used design as critique. The tools of branding and marketing were turned back on the visitor, making the act of consumption part of the installation itself.
